summary.intent: Hold ac.mu continuously from the Idle check through the transition to Connecting in addrConn.connect(), instead of releasing and re-acquiring it around resetTransport(), to close a race where two concurrent connect() calls could both observe Idle and start duplicate connection attempts (grpc/grpc-go#7365); resetTransport is renamed resetTransportAndUnlock and documented to require the caller to already hold ac.mu, and updateAddrs's async reconnect call is updated to match.
summary.issue_fit: Met for the specific race the change description and issue #7365 describe: connect() now holds ac.mu continuously into resetTransportAndUnlock, which sets Connecting before unlocking, so a concurrent connect() can no longer observe Idle in the gap. The same lock-holding refactor in updateAddrs, however, introduces a distinct, previously-absent concurrency regression (see finding below) as a side effect of the fix.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff reviewed (clientconn.go, the only changed file, +6/-7 across 3 hunks); both call sites of the renamed function inspected; the interaction with tearDown()'s and createTransport()'s pre-existing ac.mu/GracefulClose ordering inspected. Focused tests run once at head 76ef33f4 offline: `go test .` (root package, race) pass; `go test ./test -run Test/SubConnEmpty$` (race) pass, and traced to confirm it exercises updateAddrs from a Ready addrConn with a live transport; `go test ./xds/internal/xdsclient/tests -run Test/AuthorityRevive$` (race, count=20) pass, partial corroboration of the PR's reported 100000-iteration flake fix. One must-fix concurrency candidate verified by an independent fresh-context worker and confirmed.

findings.title: Unlock ac.mu before updateAddrs's deferred GracefulClose call
findings.trigger: addrConn.updateAddrs is called with a changed address list while the addrConn already has a live ac.transport (e.g. state Ready, or reconnecting to a since-superseded address) -- a routine reconnection path, not a shutdown or error path.
findings.impact: updateAddrs no longer unlocks ac.mu before returning. Its deferred `ac.transport.GracefulClose()` -- which synchronously calls the transport's onClose closure, which does `ac.mu.Lock()` -- now runs while ac.mu is still logically locked by this same goroutine, so the goroutine that called updateAddrs blocks until the independently scheduled `go ac.resetTransportAndUnlock()` goroutine happens to reach its own `ac.mu.Unlock()`. At the merge-base this deferred call always ran after an explicit `ac.mu.Unlock()`, so the caller never blocked here; grpc's own tearDown() still documents and follows exactly this ac.mu/GracefulClose ordering requirement (clientconn.go:1573-1575: "We have to release the lock before the call to GracefulClose/Close here because both of them call onClose(), which requires locking ac.mu."). The block is bounded -- resetTransportAndUnlock's pre-unlock work is pure computation, no I/O -- but it is a genuine, previously nonexistent synchronization dependency on the shared address-update path.
findings.change: Before updateAddrs returns, unlock ac.mu explicitly (as at the merge-base) so the deferred GracefulClose always runs unlocked, and have the spawned reconnect goroutine acquire ac.mu itself at entry instead of assuming the caller's lock carries over; do not rely on the spawned goroutine's own unlock as the release mechanism for this goroutine's deferred call.

requirements.evidence: clientconn.go:904-919 (RIGHT): connect() holds ac.mu continuously from the Idle check into resetTransportAndUnlock(), which sets Connecting (clientconn.go:1259-1261) before unlocking, closing the double-connect-attempt race issue #7365's comment 3 describes.

The PR's "Tested" claim (100000 attempts of Test/AuthorityRevive without flaking) cannot be reproduced offline within the 5-minute focused-command bound. Ran `go test google.golang.org/grpc/xds/internal/xdsclient/tests -run 'Test/AuthorityRevive$' -race -count=20` at head 76ef33f4: 20/20 pass, consistent with but not independently conclusive corroboration of the reported flake elimination at ~0.4% baseline flake rate.

The orphaned-transport race the release note describes (arjan-bal's comment: only one transport closed on subConn update, the other orphaned until server shutdown) is fixed for connect() by the continuous-lock change (clientconn.go:904-919). The same refactor, applied to updateAddrs, introduces a related but distinct new concurrency issue -- finding clientconn/updateaddrs-gracefulclose-lock-contention -- so the release note's implicit promise of a clean fix with no new synchronization side effects is only partially met.
